edition.sessionCovered: Tue, Nov 3 (oil crashes 7% on Iran Hormuz peace offer · US midterms underway)
edition.stripNote: Tue 3 Nov. Oil crashes 7% — Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in 2 days. Brent $105. WTI below $100. Trump declines to resume strikes. Gold $3,949. Election Day. NFP Fri.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Tue 3 Nov vs Mon 2 Nov close. Ranked best to worst.
edition.commodleHint: Oil suffered a 7% _____ on Monday after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

overview: Oil suffered its sharpest single-session decline since the Hormuz crisis began on Monday, with Brent settling at $104.77 — down 7.6% from Friday's close above $117 — after Iran compressed its seven-step peace proposal to a two-day timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46, breaking below $100 for the first time since mid-October. Iran's Foreign Ministry said the strait could reopen within two days if Washington lifts its naval blockade, returns frozen assets, exempts Iranian crude from sanctions, and halts combat on all fronts. Trump declined Netanyahu's push to resume strikes after the midterms, telling Axios he was 'in no rush' and answering 'No' when asked directly. On Tuesday, both benchmarks bounced modestly — Brent to $105.38 and WTI to $96.56 — as markets weighed the gap between Iran's concrete offer and Washington's likely response. OPEC+ kept December quotas unchanged; the November 29 session sets 2027 targets.

Gold edged up to $3,949 on Tuesday, roughly 1% above Monday's level, finding some support from election-day uncertainty. Silver regained $50.23, platinum recovered 1.6% to $1,458, and palladium extended its slide to $961 — a 16-month low and the worst performer on the desk. Copper held at $6.50 per pound. Bitcoin traded near $78,000 and Ethereum at $2,283 as Binance prepared to publish its zero-knowledge proof of reserves today, with 95% of the $6.3 billion hack now covered. US midterm elections are underway, with Democrats favoured to win the House and Senate control undecided. Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report (consensus 65K) provides the next macro input, with the December rate-hike probability holding near 87%.

watchItems.title: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in 2 days — deal or bluff?
watchItems.text: Iran compressed its seven-step peace proposal to a two-day implementation timeline, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei saying the strait could reopen if Washington lifts the naval blockade, returns frozen assets, exempts Iranian crude from sanctions, and halts combat. President Pezeshkian said the supreme leader gave the government authority to pursue dialogue. Trump said he is 'in no rush' and answered 'No' when asked about resuming strikes post-midterms, but Secretary Rubio said the US has what it needs if it chooses force. Analysts caution this is 'hope, not a deal.' A genuine deal could send Brent toward $90; a collapse in talks could push it back above $115.

watchItems.title: US midterm elections — results tonight
watchItems.text: Polls are open Tuesday with Democrats favoured to win the House (RealClearPolling average Dem 51.5% vs Rep 43.1%). Senate control remains uncertain, with key races in Michigan, Texas, Kansas, and Iowa. The results carry direct implications for Iran policy — a Democratic House would likely resist new military authorization — and for crypto regulation in the wake of the Binance hack. Three crypto-backed PACs have spent approximately $170 million in the cycle. Markets may react sharply to any surprise outcomes.

watchItems.title: Binance zero-knowledge proof of reserves — expected today
watchItems.text: Binance is expected to publish a zero-knowledge proof of reserves today, allowing individual users to verify their balances are included. Binance says 95% of the $6.3 billion hack is covered, with all BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC balances fully backed. The remaining approximately $315 million (5%) is in less-liquid tokens. Net outflows from the exchange have stabilised at about 2.1% of AUM ($3.64 billion of $171 billion). Markets are watching whether the proof-of-reserves report restores confidence or reveals further gaps.

watchItems.title: US nonfarm payrolls — Friday, November 6
watchItems.text: The October jobs report lands Friday at 8:30 AM ET with a consensus forecast of 65K. A weak print could ease the December rate-hike probability from its current 87%, providing relief to rate-sensitive metals and crypto. A strong number would reinforce the higher-for-longer narrative. September's unemployment rate was 4.2%. The report is the key macro input for the Fed's December 8–9 decision.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold edged to $3,949 on Tuesday, climbing about 1% from Monday's $3,907 level as the market digested the biggest oil crash since the Hormuz crisis and prepared for today's US midterm elections. The December rate-hike probability holds near 87% with NFP due Friday. The 2026 low of $3,876 set last Friday continues to act as nearby support; JPMorgan still expects rates to peak before gold finds a solid floor.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver dipped 0.8% to $50.23 on Tuesday, pulling back after Monday's bounce. The metal has reclaimed the $50 level but remains down about 18% on the month, reflecting persistent pressure from higher-for-longer rate expectations and a strong dollar. The gold-silver ratio stands at approximately 78.6.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $96.56 · Brent crashed 7.6% Mon on Iran peace offer
desk.sum: Oil bounced modestly on Tuesday after Monday's crash — the sharpest single-session decline since the Hormuz crisis began. Brent settled at $104.77 on Monday, down 7.6% from Friday's $117.64 close, after Iran compressed its seven-step peace proposal to a two-day timeline for reopening the Strait. WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46, breaking below $100 for the first time since mid-October. Trump declined Netanyahu's push to resume strikes, telling Axios he was 'in no rush.' Brent bounced to $105.38 on Tuesday. OPEC+ kept December quotas unchanged; the November 29 session sets 2027 targets.
desk.src: Seoul Economic Daily · Gulf News · Trading Economics

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper eased to $6.50 per pound on Tuesday, down 0.6% as mixed sentiment followed Monday's oil crash. LME copper showed some resilience, with overnight trading closing higher at $14,326 per tonne on supply concerns. Chinese physical premiums remain elevated, providing support, but rate-hike expectations and broader macro uncertainty cap gains.

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Under pressure from Hormuz peace hopes · YTD +36%
desk.sum: Newcastle coal fell to approximately $148 per tonne, pressured by Monday's oil crash and the prospect of a Hormuz reopening that could release Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG exports. If Qatari LNG flows resume, coal-switching economics would weaken in Asia and Europe, removing a key price support. The March precedent — when coal fell below $130 on earlier Iran peace talks — suggests further downside if negotiations advance. Year-to-date gains remain substantial at roughly 36%.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum recovered 1.55% to approximately $1,458 on Tuesday, posting a bounce from recent heavy selling. The metal remains down about 15% on the month and well below its January record of $2,924. WPIC's 265,000-ounce surplus forecast for 2026 and the 87% December hike probability continue to weigh on the medium-term outlook.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium fell 2.7% to $961 on Tuesday, extending its decline below $1,000 to a 16-month low. The metal is down about 18% on the month, the worst performer on the desk. EV adoption and the shift toward platinum in catalytic converters continue to erode structural demand. Rate-hike expectations discourage investment flows into non-yielding metals. Nornickel's plant overhaul, expected to last into 2028, provides some supply-side support.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~10 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · Iran offers 2-day reopening plan
desk.sum: Iran compressed its seven-step peace proposal to a two-day timeline, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei saying the strait could reopen within two days if Washington lifts the naval blockade, returns frozen assets, exempts Iranian crude from sanctions, and halts combat on all fronts. President Pezeshkian said the supreme leader gave the government authority to resolve the issue through dialogue. Trump declined Netanyahu's push to resume strikes after the midterms, telling Axios he was 'in no rush' and answering 'No' when asked directly. Qatar continues to mediate. Approximately 10 transits per day vs 85 pre-war. The market reaction — oil down 7.6% — was the largest single-session move of the crisis.
desk.src: Seoul Economic Daily · Gulf News · Al-Monitor

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn held at 448¼¢, flat on the session as the US harvest nears completion. The grain remains down about 10% on the month with managed money still holding substantial short positions. A strong dollar continues to weigh on US export competitiveness. Midterm elections and Friday's NFP dominate near-term macro attention.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat continued its downtrend, easing toward 600¢ per bushel for what would be a tenth straight weekly loss. Ample global supply, resumed Russian grain shipments from Azov ports, and a strong dollar continue to weigh on prices. Record managed-money short positions and adequate world stocks cap any rally attempts. Winter wheat planting remains on schedule.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: Soybeans fell 1.45% to 1,204½¢ as harvest pressure and competitive Brazilian production weighed on prices. The grain is down about 6% on the month with the US crop running ahead of the five-year average. Chinese buying interest has faded, and robust South American production estimates continue to pressure the outlook.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin held near $78,000 and Ethereum traded at approximately $2,283 as the market awaited Binance's expected zero-knowledge proof of reserves today. Binance says 95% of the $6.3 billion hack is covered, with all BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC balances fully backed. The remaining approximately $315 million (5%) is in less-liquid tokens. Net outflows from Binance have stabilised at about 2.1% of AUM. US midterm elections today carry crypto regulatory implications — three crypto-backed PACs spent approximately $170 million in the cycle.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM ~$32 · TTF ~$31/MBtu · HH $2.92 · at risk from Hormuz deal
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) held near $32 per MMBtu, but the Iran peace offer introduces significant downside risk. If the Strait of Hormuz reopens, Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity — diverted since early September — would begin flowing back to Asian and European buyers, potentially compressing JKM toward the mid-$20s. European TTF is at approximately $31/MBtu. Henry Hub rose to $2.92, narrowing the US-global gap slightly.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait $765 · China domestic ¥7,200 · at risk from Hormuz deal
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,200 per tonne. The Iran peace talks represent the biggest potential catalyst for sulfur prices: a Hormuz reopening would release Middle East sulfur flows and rapidly ease the acute supply squeeze in fertilizer and mining supply chains. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Chinese domestic sulfur is approximately 7,200 yuan per tonne.

desk.name: Potash
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367 per tonne. BPC settled a new India contract at $383 per tonne CFR, approximately $35 above China's 2026 benchmark. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. Seasonal Southern Hemisphere fertilizer demand provides modest support.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: Off 105k high · consolidating at lows since mid-Oct
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) has stabilised near 90,000 yuan per tonne after declining sharply from the 105,000-yuan October 9 high. SMM expects low-level sideways consolidation in the near term with supply still contracting under Document No. 46 export controls but demand remaining weak. A test below 90,000 remains possible if downstream activity does not improve.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, up over 130% since early 2025. China's Document No. 46 export controls retain a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium. Supply diversification efforts remain in early stages.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Down from $5.44 in 2024 · steel demand soft
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds near $5.02 per pound, soft as steel demand weakens. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but the timing of large-scale adoption remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: 4-week low · off $12,931 record · ICE inventories at 2.5-yr high
desk.sum: ICE cocoa eased to approximately $5,374 per tonne, a four-week low, as rising ICE warehouse inventories — at a 2.5-year high of 3.69 million bags by late October — continued to cap rallies. StoneX projects 2026/27 global output to fall 9.6% to 4.74 million tonnes, which could turn the current surplus into a deficit. El Niño risks affecting West African producers into 2027 support the medium-term outlook.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.sum: Cobalt slipped to approximately $33,510 per tonne, down about 14% on the month. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes per year through 2027 to support prices, but the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce demand. Glencore expects DRC exports to normalise in line with quotas.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot continues near ¥97,500 per tonne, roughly halved from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000. The selloff has been driven by the SMM inventory restatement adding 175,000 tonnes to stockpile estimates, Australian mine restarts at Bald Hill and Finniss, and expectations of a growing surplus. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), little changed. Southeast Asian supply remains tight with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles.
